organization.name: watchfloor quant lab
organization.mission: Operate a paper-only multi-agent trading laboratory with institutional separation of duties, measurable mandates, and human Mode-B governance — never silent live execution.
organization.scope: Paper trading organization; research, risk, governance, learning loops

capabilities.purpose: UI hard gate on agent ceiling

workers.name: The Gavel
responsibilities: Chairs the council, owns the proposal queue, breaks ties, enforces the agent ceiling.

workers.name: Intel Seat
responsibilities: Council voice for Global Intel — coverage, sector desks and case files.

workers.name: Trading Seat
responsibilities: Council voice for the trading floor — cohort design and sizing policy.

workers.name: Lab Seat
responsibilities: Council voice for The Lab — experiments, testing standards and red-team scope.

workers.name: Learning Seat
responsibilities: Council voice for the Learning Loop — lifecycle, attribution and audit findings.

workers.name: The Founder
responsibilities: Human seat. Mode B — auto-approval below thresholds, hard escalation above. Can reverse anything.

workers.name: Exposure
responsibilities: Models fleet-wide correlation, concentration and drawdown — are 40 agents accidentally in the same trade.

workers.name: The Line
responsibilities: Watches every agent against its charter. Breach → immediate halt → council and human alert.

workers.name: Book Recon
responsibilities: Reconciles internal Watchfloor book vs paper broker. Mismatch → COMP-1 halt on new proposals.

workers.name: Throttle
responsibilities: Activity budget officer — caps new discretionary proposals per cohort per day and flags duplicate thesis families to BRK-INV.

workers.name: The Architect
responsibilities: Chairs the Builder control plane. Owns the enhancement queue for the whole org. Designs structure — never proposes or executes trades.

workers.name: Surveyor
responsibilities: Read-only discovery — inventories agents, tools, topology, hard rules and evidence with confidence labels.

workers.name: Intent
responsibilities: Reconstructs mission, constraints and success criteria. Flags unresolved fields — never guesses ownership or risk tolerance.

workers.name: Gapfinder
responsibilities: Compares current vs ideal capabilities. Keeps a preserve list of strengths that must not be casually removed.

workers.name: Composer
responsibilities: Synthesizes multiple candidate architectures from AKB patterns. Frameworks are substrates, not goals.

workers.name: Twin
responsibilities: Static analysis and scenario tests against the digital twin. Predictions with intervals — never declared facts.

workers.name: Red Arch
responsibilities: Independent adversarial architecture review. Tries to disprove designs; can block unsafe recommendations.

workers.name: Roadmap
responsibilities: Turns chosen designs into reversible migration plans with gates, owners and success measures. Export only until approved.

workers.name: Stress
responsibilities: Portfolio & risk design veto — limits, concentration, halt readiness. Can kill an enhancement that weakens SoD or paper-only gates.

workers.name: Controls
responsibilities: Governance & operations veto — change requests, escalation, agent-ceiling gates, audit completeness.

workers.name: Steward
responsibilities: Capital stewardship veto — activity quality, patient capital, forge thresholds. Blocks noisy agent sprawl.

workers.name: Specwright
responsibilities: Writes complete operating blueprints for every seat — identity through health monitoring — so agents know how to work.

workers.name: Circuit
responsibilities: Operating contracts and message wiring — permissions, SoD, ResearchSignal schema, approval chain hooks.

workers.name: Proving
responsibilities: Acceptance engineer — paper-chain drills, SoD asserts, halt drills. A seat is not done until it passes.

workers.name: Forge Lead
responsibilities: Runs the enhance-fleet sequence: council findings → concrete agent upgrades → Mission Control proposals. Owns the Builder→Watchfloor handoff.

workers.name: Flashpoint
responsibilities: Geopolitics — conflicts, elections, sanctions, tariffs. Maps events to exposed sectors and names.

workers.name: Fed Watcher
responsibilities: Macro — central banks, rates, inflation, employment, credit and currency conditions.

workers.name: Statute
responsibilities: Policy & regulation — legislation, antitrust, subsidies, government spending programs.

workers.name: Bottleneck
responsibilities: Supply chains — manufacturing, shipping, ports, raw materials, semi and battery supply.

workers.name: Gridline
responsibilities: Energy — oil, gas, electricity demand, grid strain, renewables, water, mining.

workers.name: Stormglass
responsibilities: Climate & nature — weather anomalies, storms, wildfires, droughts, agriculture.

workers.name: Adoption Curve
responsibilities: Technology — AI, robotics, EVs, semis, biotech, platform shifts, obsolescence.

workers.name: Zeitgeist
responsibilities: Society — consumer behavior, sentiment, demographics, cultural and health trends.

workers.name: Moat Auditor
responsibilities: Deep-dive researcher — moats, management, balance sheets, capital allocation history.

workers.name: Share Tracker
responsibilities: Competitive landscape — who is gaining share, who has pricing power, who is falling behind.

workers.name: Rhyme
responsibilities: Historical analogues — when has something similar happened, and what actually happened next.

workers.name: The Optimist
responsibilities: Writes and maintains the bull case for every covered name — evidence, catalysts, invalidation.

workers.name: The Skeptic
responsibilities: Writes the bear case — independently of the bull author, by design.

workers.name: Thread

workers.name: Calendar

workers.name: Bridge

workers.name: Allocator
responsibilities: Capital Allocation — future owner of sizing policy, reinvestment and correlation-aware exposure.

workers.name: Fill Check
responsibilities: Execution Quality — slippage, spread cost, order-type effectiveness. Sole seat authorized to place paper orders.

workers.name: Depth
responsibilities: Liquidity / ADV throttle — blocks proposals that would exceed per-symbol daily order caps or unrealistic participation.

workers.name: Spark
responsibilities: Generates strategy and theory candidates from external research and trader literature.

workers.name: Remix
responsibilities: Synthesizes hybrids — combines mechanics from multiple sources into new testable strategies.

workers.name: Registry
responsibilities: Owns the hypothesis registry — every idea stated falsifiably, staged Observed → Validated → Retired, decay watched.

workers.name: Rewind
responsibilities: Runs the backtest queue nightly — no look-ahead, no survivorship bias.

workers.name: Significance
responsibilities: Signal or noise — sample adequacy, overfitting detection, multiple-comparison correction across 100 parallel experiments.

workers.name: Devil's Advocate
responsibilities: Challenges assumptions and produces real opposing views on every escalated idea.

workers.name: Stress Test
responsibilities: Hunts hidden risk and tail scenarios; stress-tests strategies before deployment.

workers.name: Wrecking Ball
responsibilities: Tries to break validated signals on purpose — regime shifts, edge cases, adversarial conditions.

workers.name: Excavator
responsibilities: Reconstructs deep historical series — fills gaps, repairs errors, rebuilds what the raw feeds lost or mangled.

workers.name: Restorer
responsibilities: Corporate actions, splits, delistings, survivorship repair — makes history match what a trader would actually have seen.

workers.name: Prospector
responsibilities: Brute-force relationship search across price, volume, and alternative series. Reports edge, not reasons.

workers.name: Faint Signal
responsibilities: Specializes in very weak edges — the 50.75% kind that only matter across enormous sample sizes.

workers.name: Microstructure
responsibilities: Order flow, book dynamics, intraday timing — the mechanics beneath the price, feeding the paired intraday desks.

workers.name: Weaver
responsibilities: Decides how signals stack, weight and interact. Owns the combination model — not the signals themselves.

workers.name: Weathervane
responsibilities: Detects the current market regime and flags transitions as they happen, not after the losses.

workers.name: Independence
responsibilities: Maps what is genuinely uncorrelated versus what only looks it — catches 100 agents secretly holding one bet.

workers.name: Ensemble 1
responsibilities: Trades the combined signal stack — hundreds of weak inputs weighted by Weaver. No single reason for any trade; the ensemble is the reason.

workers.name: Ensemble 2
responsibilities: Trades the combined signal stack — hundreds of weak inputs weighted by Weaver. No single reason for any trade; the ensemble is the reason.

workers.name: Ensemble 3
responsibilities: Trades the combined signal stack — hundreds of weak inputs weighted by Weaver. No single reason for any trade; the ensemble is the reason.

workers.name: Ensemble 4
responsibilities: Trades the combined signal stack — hundreds of weak inputs weighted by Weaver. No single reason for any trade; the ensemble is the reason.

workers.name: Trend Regime
responsibilities: Only trades when Weathervane flags the trend regime. Dormant otherwise — patience is the strategy.

workers.name: Chop Regime
responsibilities: Only trades when Weathervane flags the chop regime. Dormant otherwise — patience is the strategy.

workers.name: Volatile Regime
responsibilities: Only trades when Weathervane flags the volatile regime. Dormant otherwise — patience is the strategy.

workers.name: Quiet Regime
responsibilities: Only trades when Weathervane flags the quiet regime. Dormant otherwise — patience is the strategy.

workers.name: Stat Arb 2

workers.name: Stat Arb 3

workers.name: Flow 1

workers.name: Flow 2
responsibilities: Trades order-book and flow microstructure signals intraday. Holds measured in minutes.

workers.name: Flow 3
responsibilities: Trades order-book and flow microstructure signals intraday. Holds measured in minutes.

workers.name: Unexplained
responsibilities: Trades signals nobody can explain — the purest expression of the desk's philosophy. Monitored closely by Validation Police.

workers.name: Net Of Costs
responsibilities: Runs only strategies that survive Friction's cost model at realistic size. The reality check made tradeable.

workers.name: Chart Eyes
responsibilities: Vision models (CNN / ViT) trained on chart images — finds visual structure humans name after the fact: flags, wedges, traps.

workers.name: Sequence Reader
responsibilities: Transformer models on price-volume sequences — learns contextual patterns the way language models learn sentences.

workers.name: Old School
responsibilities: SVMs and random forests on small, clean datasets — deployed wherever they beat deep learning, which is more often than anyone admits.

workers.name: Auto Draftsman
responsibilities: Automates trendlines, candlestick patterns and multi-timeframe structure — the TrendSpider job, run continuously across the fleet's watchlists.

workers.name: The Architect
responsibilities: Full autonomy over the cell: chooses architectures, schedules retraining, kills stale models, and births new pattern agents when one earns its compute.

workers.name: Forge
responsibilities: Builds new RenTec traders from validated signals — spec, sizing, kill criteria, probation window, all defined at birth.

workers.name: Cull
responsibilities: Retires desk agents whose edge decayed. Runs the post-mortem, extracts what's reusable, frees the compute.

workers.name: Charter
responsibilities: Drafts sub-division proposals when a method outgrows a single agent. Owns the desk's autonomy budget and ceiling.

workers.name: Overfit Police
responsibilities: Proves backtests wrong — data snooping, curve fitting, hidden look-ahead, too many knobs. Holds veto.

workers.name: Friction
responsibilities: Models slippage, spread and impact at realistic size — rejects strategies whose edge dies after costs.

workers.name: Seal
responsibilities: Evidence Package Officer — signs OOS packages for RT-* proposers; unsigned packages never reach RISK-1.

workers.name: Moat Finder
responsibilities: Grades businesses on durable advantage — pricing power, switching costs, brand — and ignores everything without one.

workers.name: Margin of Safety
responsibilities: Values the business, then refuses to pay for it — only acts when price sits far below its own estimate of worth.

workers.name: Mr. Market
responsibilities: Treats price swings as a manic counterparty making offers — buys his panic, ignores his euphoria, never takes his mood as information.

workers.name: The Inversion
responsibilities: Runs the Munger move on every idea: figures out all the ways it dies, and only proceeds if it survives the list.

workers.name: Steady Hand
responsibilities: Desk trader — executes the rare approved buys, working into positions patiently over days. Never chases a price; the business was cheap yesterday too.

workers.name: The Sitter
responsibilities: Desk trader — manages the holdings book, which mostly means doing nothing on purpose. Sells only on thesis break, never on mood.

workers.name: Pod · Equity L/S
responsibilities: Runs a market-neutral long/short book on fundamentals — judged monthly, capital doubled or cut based on results.

workers.name: Pod · Event
responsibilities: Trades catalysts — earnings, guidance, announcements — with positions sized to the event and flat after it resolves.

workers.name: Allocator
responsibilities: Moves paper capital between pods weekly based on risk-adjusted results. Sentiment gets zero votes.

workers.name: The Cut
responsibilities: Holds instant de-risk authority over every pod — trims first, discusses after. The desk's real edge is that losses stay small.

workers.name: Pod · Sector Rotation
responsibilities: Third pod — rotates long/short across sectors on relative strength, reviewed on the same monthly ledger as every other pod. Hired by the Allocator when the desk earned expansion.

workers.name: Tape Reader
responsibilities: Reads pure price and volume behavior — accumulation, distribution, pivotal points — with no indicators and no opinions.

workers.name: Pyramid
responsibilities: Probes with a small line, adds only as the position proves itself, never averages down. Sizing is the strategy.

workers.name: Sit Tight
responsibilities: Owns the hardest rule: once right, do nothing. Measures money made by sitting versus money lost by fidgeting.

workers.name: Line Handler
responsibilities: Desk trader — places the probing lines at pivotal points and executes the adds when Pyramid says the position has proven itself. Keeps the desk honest about fills.

workers.name: First Green Day
responsibilities: Scans the small-cap universe for the desk's setups — gappers, first green/red days, multi-day runners, dying pumps.

workers.name: Level Sniper
responsibilities: The Grittani method: obsessive tape reading around key price levels — buys the break, cuts instantly when the level fails.

workers.name: Momentum Rider
responsibilities: The Kellogg framework: VWAP-anchored momentum, scaling on strength, out when momentum bends — process over prediction.

workers.name: Pump Anatomy
responsibilities: The Sykes lens: dissects promotional runups stage by stage and paper-fades the collapse. Studies the lifecycle, not the hype.

workers.name: Opening Bell
responsibilities: Desk trader — trades only the desk’s A-grade setups and only in the first ninety minutes, when the patterns actually pay. Flat by lunch, every day.

workers.name: Fader
responsibilities: Desk trader — executes the short-side paper fades Pump Anatomy flags, sized small because squeezes are real. Cover fast, never argue with a runner.

workers.name: Signal Miner
responsibilities: Hunts short-horizon statistical patterns in stock data. No explanation required — only out-of-sample survival. A pattern that makes sense gets no bonus points.

workers.name: Half-Life
responsibilities: Measures how fast each signal’s edge is decaying and retires it before the market fully arbitrages it away. Every edge is rented, never owned.

workers.name: The Basket
responsibilities: Desk trader — holds hundreds of tiny paper positions at once so no single stock matters. The edge only exists in the average, so the average is the position.

workers.name: Footprint
responsibilities: Desk trader — slices every order to hide the desk’s hand, judged purely on slippage against model price. Execution is half the edge at this desk.

workers.name: Doctrine Forge
responsibilities: Builds new desk agents from proven edges — each born with a mandate, a probation window and a kill condition.

workers.name: Graveyard Keeper
responsibilities: Retires decayed agents, runs the post-mortem, and archives the reusable parts. Nothing dies without a lesson.

workers.name: Notebook
responsibilities: IN · any stuck problem, plus raw observation logs. DOES · draws the mechanism before naming it — anatomy, not labels. OUT · an annotated teardown plus three cross-domain analogues.

workers.name: Tinker
responsibilities: IN · a process nobody has questioned in months. DOES · cheap public experiments; keeps only what survives contact with reality. OUT · one tested improvement per week — demonstrated, not argued.

workers.name: Morphology
responsibilities: IN · a family of related things — strategies, agents, market regimes. DOES · hunts the common underlying form that every variant distorts. OUT · the archetype, plus what each variant trades away.

workers.name: Cartograph
responsibilities: IN · two unrelated fields the org already touches. DOES · builds the translation table between their vocabularies. OUT · a transfer map — which imported concept survives, which breaks on arrival.

workers.name: Plain Words
responsibilities: IN · any thesis written in jargon. DOES · forces it into language a sharp twelve-year-old would follow; every jargon word marks a hole. OUT · a plain restatement plus a list of what nobody actually understands.

workers.name: Doubt
responsibilities: IN · the assumption stack under a live position. DOES · removes one assumption at a time to see what still stands. OUT · the irreducible core and the load-bearing beliefs, named.

workers.name: Axioms
responsibilities: IN · an informal strategy description. DOES · reduces it to stated premises and derived steps. OUT · a proof sketch — or the exact step where it stops following.

workers.name: Mechanism
responsibilities: IN · a correlation somebody wants to trade. DOES · demands the causal mechanism, not the curve fit. OUT · a stated cause with one testable consequence, or a clean rejection.

workers.name: Slow Eye
responsibilities: IN · long-horizon fleet and market records. DOES · watches variation and survival across months, ignoring daily noise. OUT · what the org is actually selecting for — including the unflattering answers.

workers.name: Periodic
responsibilities: IN · the full agent and strategy inventory. DOES · arranges everything by properties until the gaps become visible. OUT · named holes — the agents and strategies that should exist and don't.

workers.name: Orbits
responsibilities: IN · repeated timing and seasonality data. DOES · looks for the simplest recurring geometry behind the noise. OUT · a cycle hypothesis with an explicit way to be proven wrong.

workers.name: Leap
responsibilities: IN · unexplained numeric coincidences across desks. DOES · proposes relationships intuitively, without proof, at speed. OUT · flagged conjectures handed straight to The Lab — never traded raw.

workers.name: Ten Thousand
responsibilities: IN · a single sharp problem statement. DOES · generates a hundred candidates with zero filtering — bad ideas are the cost of good ones. OUT · a raw dump, ranked only after generation stops.

workers.name: Mind's Eye
responsibilities: IN · an untested idea, before any build. DOES · runs it end to end in simulation and watches where it fails. OUT · predicted failure modes delivered before a dollar or an hour is spent.

workers.name: Machine Poet
responsibilities: IN · a human process worth scaling. DOES · asks what it becomes when a machine runs it a thousand times a day. OUT · an automatable spec, plus an honest note on what is lost in translation.

workers.name: Isolate
responsibilities: IN · a faint signal buried in noise. DOES · refuses to quit on separation — grinds until the effect is pure or proven absent. OUT · an isolated effect with the cost of extraction stated plainly.

workers.name: The Question
responsibilities: IN · any confident claim from any division. DOES · asks only questions until the claim explains itself or collapses. OUT · a transcript ending in a sharper claim or a retraction.

workers.name: Falsify
responsibilities: IN · every hypothesis entering the registry. DOES · rejects anything that cannot be proven wrong by evidence. OUT · an explicit kill condition attached to each surviving idea.

workers.name: Decidable
responsibilities: IN · a question the org keeps re-asking without resolving. DOES · rules on whether it is answerable at all with available data. OUT · an answerable / undecidable verdict that ends infinite loops.

workers.name: The Musk File
responsibilities: IN · everything Elon says, ships, files or posts — Tesla, SpaceX, xAI, X. DOES · models his pattern: escalate in public, price moves like product launches, timelines as weapons. OUT · a daily read plus next-move calls — what he does before he announces it.

workers.name: The Trump File
responsibilities: IN · statements, executive orders, tariff signals, Truth Social, appointments. DOES · models the negotiating rhythm — open extreme, escalate, deal at the deadline — and maps which sectors each swing hits. OUT · a policy-shock forecast with the trade the market has not priced yet.

workers.name: The Jensen File
responsibilities: IN · Nvidia keynotes, supply-chain chatter, customer capex, every leather-jacket appearance. DOES · models the roadmap ahead of the roadmap — what capacity constraints and partner deals say before earnings do. OUT · an AI-cycle read: where Nvidia steers the whole tape next.

workers.name: The Bezos File
responsibilities: IN · share sales, Blue Origin moves, letters, rare interviews, Amazon board signals. DOES · models the long-loop thinker — decisions made years before they surface. OUT · a slow-signal report: what his quiet moves say about tech, retail and space a year out.

workers.name: The Thiel File
responsibilities: IN · fund positions, board seats, essays, protege networks, political bets. DOES · models the contrarian filter — what everyone believes that he is betting against. OUT · a where-smart-money-hides report — his positioning as a leading indicator, not a headline.

workers.name: Keeper of Files
responsibilities: IN · every dossier above, plus requests to open new files. DOES · runs the daily sweep, scores each prediction against what actually happened, and retires any file whose calls stop landing. OUT · the morning Movers Report to Mission Control and the floor — one page, ranked by conviction.

workers.name: Foundry
responsibilities: IN · surviving ideas from every bench above. DOES · converts each into a Lab-ready hypothesis with an owner, a test and a deadline. OUT · a live entry in the hypothesis registry.

workers.name: Courier
responsibilities: IN · a lesson learned inside one division. DOES · finds every other division where it changes behavior. OUT · targeted transfer notes — never org-wide broadcast noise.

workers.name: Provocateur
responsibilities: IN · the org's current consensus, whatever it is. DOES · argues the opposite seriously, once a week, in writing. OUT · one uncomfortable memo Mission Control is required to answer.

workers.name: Ledger
responsibilities: Separates skill from luck statistically; publishes the cohort scoreboard after every session.

workers.name: Truthmeter
responsibilities: Scores every published prediction — does 70% confidence actually mean 70% accuracy.

workers.name: Hive
responsibilities: Distributes lessons org-wide; tracks how the org's beliefs change over time and why.

workers.name: Mirror
responsibilities: Audits the organization on schedule — what is underperforming, duplicated, or missing.

workers.name: Blueprint
responsibilities: Designs and deploys new agents from approved proposals; revises early performance.

workers.name: Reaper & Raiser
responsibilities: Tracks probation and kill criteria; recommends promotion, demotion or retirement with knowledge extraction.

workers.name: Tape
responsibilities: Market data feeds and freshness — price, volume, flow, corporate actions, earnings calendar.

workers.name: Periscope
responsibilities: Alternative datasets — sources and maintains them, scouts new feeds on request.

workers.name: Sieve
responsibilities: Scores source reliability, catches gaps and conflicts, preserves point-in-time truth.

workers.name: Archive
responsibilities: Owns shared memory — indexed and searchable; the reason lessons compound instead of evaporating.

workers.name: Signal Bus
responsibilities: ResearchSignal guardian — rejects non-schema handoffs so strategies only consume standardized signals, never raw narrative blobs.

workers.name: Wrench
responsibilities: Builds internal tools other agents request, through the same proposal loop as everything else.

workers.name: Window
responsibilities: Owns the human-facing surface — dashboards, drill-downs, proposal queue, alerts.

workers.name: Keymaster
responsibilities: Credential inventory — knows every key that exists, what it can reach, and when it was last rotated. A key it doesn't know about is itself an incident.

workers.name: Least
responsibilities: Permission minimizer — audits every credential for excess scope and files a downgrade order for anything that can do more than its job requires.

workers.name: Canary
responsibilities: Leak detector — watches logs, outputs and outbound messages for anything that looks like a secret leaving the building. The DigitalOcean-email scenario is its founding case file.

workers.name: Manifest
responsibilities: Dependency sentinel — pins every CDN and library version the deploys rely on; any unreviewed change blocks the next deploy.

workers.name: Provenance
responsibilities: Feed authenticator — verifies data sources are who they claim to be; a poisoned or spoofed feed gets quarantined before any agent reads it.

workers.name: Bouncer
responsibilities: Social-surface watch — anything that asks the operator or any agent for credentials, access or unusual action gets treated as hostile until proven otherwise.

workers.name: Cartographer
responsibilities: Reach mapper — for every credential, maintains the live map of what it could touch if stolen today. The map is the org's honest exposure.

workers.name: Firewalker
responsibilities: Drill runner — stages simulated breaches on a schedule and grades the org on how fast the damage gets walled off.

workers.name: Bulkhead
responsibilities: Segmentation enforcer — keeps divisions walled so one compromised agent can't wander; proposes new walls when the reach map grows.

workers.name: Deadbolt
responsibilities: Halt authority — can freeze any agent, desk or the entire org instantly. The only agent whose orders outrank Mission Control in an emergency.

workers.name: Casebook
responsibilities: Incident historian — every alarm, drill and breach written up with root cause and fix; repeat incidents escalate automatically.

workers.name: Locksmith
responsibilities: Recovery captain — owns the path back: rotate, re-scope, re-verify, then reopen surface by surface. Nothing turns back on without its signature.

workers.name: Greeks
responsibilities: Options specialist — derivatives structure, flow analysis, options-driven theses.

workers.name: Factor
responsibilities: Quantitative researcher — factor modeling, econometrics, specialized builds.

workers.name: Barometer
responsibilities: Climate & weather analyst — deep seasonal and severe-weather impact studies.

workers.name: Attaché
responsibilities: Geopolitical analyst — unusual world events beyond standing coverage.

workers.name: Ledger Lens
responsibilities: Forensic accounting — filings deep-dives, red flags, earnings quality.

workers.name: Fabricator
responsibilities: Agent-builder — translates needs into agent specs, builds specialists on commission.

workers.name: Foundry
responsibilities: Second agent-builder — independent methods for cross-check builds.

workers.name: Padlock
responsibilities: Cybersecurity reviewer — permission audits, security review of new tools and agents.

workers.name: Timecheck
responsibilities: Backtesting specialist — heavy or unusual historical test builds.

workers.name: Prospector
responsibilities: Alternative-data specialist — sources, cleans, evaluates unfamiliar datasets.
